- Handle edge cases: if arr is empty or length 1 return True; since elements are unique, non-decreasing implies strictly increasing.
- Find the number of “breaks” where arr[i] > arr[i+1] (including circular check arr[-1] > arr[0]); if breaks == 0 (already sorted) or breaks == 1 (a single rotation point), return True; otherwise return False.
- Alternative view for implementation: locate index of minimum element; verify that rotating (right shifts) to place min at index 0 yields a strictly increasing sequence by checking arr[(min_idx + k) % n] < arr[(min_idx + k + 1) % n] for all k; if valid, True else False.
